section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the verse "He turned the sea into dry land; they will cross the river on foot; there we will rejoice in Him," linking the splitting of the sea to the future redemption and the eternal joy in His very Essence.
section.t: "He turned the sea into dry land; they will cross the river on foot; there we will rejoice in Him,"
and the explanation of this is,
"He turned the sea into dry land" is past tense, speaking of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds,
"they will cross the river on foot,"
is future tense, referring to the future to come,
that then it will be, "And He will wave His hand"
over the river with His mighty wind,
after "the Lord will utterly destroy the tongue of the Sea of Egypt,"
"and there we will rejoice" in the future "in Him,"
in His very Essence (Atzmus).
And from the fact that it connects "He turned the sea" and "they will cross the river,"
even though there is a very long time between them,
it is understood
that "He turned the sea into dry land" is the granting of the power for what will later be "they will cross the river on foot,"
and as it is written,
"As in the days of your exodus from the land of Egypt, I will show him wonders,"
that this is not merely a parallel,
but rather one depends on the other,
that the exodus from Egypt brings about the future redemption,
and therefore many details of the future redemption are learned from the redemption from Egypt.
And now, there is another explanation of this,
that the entire verse speaks of the splitting of the Sea of Reeds, for all three matters occurred at the splitting of the Sea of Reeds.
Based on this, it is simply understood that there is a connection between them,
and what is written "they will cross the river on foot" and "there we will rejoice" — in the future tense — indicates perpetuity,
for at every pilgrimage ascent there was a crossing of the river,
and also simply, the well-known river and the generic river
(in the Tanakh)
is the Euphrates River,
behold, the power for this and its beginning was at the splitting of the Sea of Reeds.
And likewise, "there we will rejoice in Him,"
for this is what happened at the splitting of the Sea of Reeds: there was the Song of the Sea, and each one pointed with his finger and said, "This is my God and I will glorify Him,"
"we will rejoice in Him," in His very Essence (Atzmus),
behold, likewise it is with every joy of a mitzvah
and the joy of the Festivals and the pilgrimage ascent, for then "every male will see" etc., specifically regarding coming to see the face of the Lord.
